summary: Dieter Schlingloff was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (1952) and habilitated at HU Berlin (1961). He held positions at Göttingen, Kiel (1968–1971), Munich (1972–1996), and Leipzig (2005).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who studied at the University of Marburg, earning his doctoral degree under supervisor Wilhelm Rau by 1970.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied under Shri Krishna Sharma and completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He served as professor at Bonn (1978–2007) and managing director of the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD 1959). He held the Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 2001.
Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsap and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, succeeding Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta. He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965–1977) and the University of Delhi (1977–1990) before serving as Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas was an Indologist and historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He later held posts at the University of Calcutta and Visva-Bharati University.

Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian who completed an M.Litt at the University of Madras and a D.Litt. at Patna University (1961). He held a teaching post at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Dina Bangdel was an art historian and religious studies scholar who held posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

Dines Andersen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He later served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian who served as Government Epigraphist for India and was Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
Dipa Ma was a Buddhist meditation teacher who studied under Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw around 1967.
Dipak Kumar Barua is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as Dean and Assistant Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta, and as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
Dipak Ranjan Das is an Indologist and historian who studied under Dineschandra Sircar and held positions at Sanskrit College and the University of Calcutta.

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who earned his PhD from the Australian National University. He taught at the University of Melbourne (circa 1983–1995) and became the Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.
Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who completed his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he subsequently served as Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.
Divyaraj Amiya is a scholar of Indology and linguistics with attested appointments at the University of Tübingen and the University of Zurich in 2026.

Diwakar Acharya is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler. He served as professor at Kyoto University (2006–2016) before becoming a professor and fellow at the University of Oxford in 2016.
Dixian was a Buddhist scholar who studied under Mingzu and served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.
